name: Oracle
description: Oracle began as a database software company and still earns most of its profit from software licences and annual support fees on databases and business applications. It has turned itself into a cloud infrastructure provider that rents data-center computing, mostly for AI training, under very large multi-year contracts: remaining contracted revenue (RPO) was $664B at August 31, 2026 against $67.4B of FY2026 revenue. To build that capacity Oracle spent $55.7B on capital equipment in FY2026 and $28.5B in the latest quarter, had free cash flow of minus $23.7B for the year, raised $43B of debt and $5B of equity in FY2026 and another $20B of stock in Q1 FY2027, and carries $125.3B of borrowings. It also sells SaaS applications (Fusion, NetSuite, Cerner health records), hardware and consulting.

gics.note: Conventional GICS label recalled from the standard scheme; not re-checked against an MSCI/S&P source. The box no longer describes the company: cloud infrastructure (renting AI computing capacity) was 27% of FY2026 revenue and 40% of Q1 FY2027 revenue, funded largely by debt.

employees.note: About 49,000 in the U.S. and 92,000 international, FY2026 10-K

businessLines.name: Cloud infrastructure (IaaS)
businessLines.how: Long-term contracts to rent GPU and computing capacity and databases-as-a-service, billed as capacity is delivered; some customers prepay for buildout. Growth is limited by how fast data centers and chips can be delivered.
businessLines.marketShare: Not sourced as a single figure. Synergy notes Oracle and neoclouds inching up; Microsoft Azure 20%, AWS 28%, Google 15% in Q2 2026

businessLines.name: Cloud applications (SaaS)
businessLines.how: Per-user annual subscriptions to finance, HR, supply-chain and NetSuite applications, and health-record systems from Cerner.

businessLines.name: Software (licence and support)
businessLines.how: Annual support fees on databases and middleware already installed, plus new and on-premise licences; revenue is slightly shrinking (-1% FY2026).

businessLines.name: Hardware
businessLines.how: One-time sales of Exadata and other servers plus support contracts.

businessLines.name: Services
businessLines.how: Consulting and implementation fees billed by project or time.
